open_points.subject: A13 edge delivery-state observability
open_points.text: “Every edge has exactly one delivery state” and required test 10 says an edge “is reported `undecided`”, but no rule says which run response, inspection result or trace exposes that state, whether all edges are included, or at what point it is reported.
open_points.question: Where and when must each edge’s derived delivery state be observable?
options: Expose every edge state in each returned or inspected run, derived from the current trace
Expose edge states only when the run has ended
Keep edge states internal and verify them only through output reasons
open_points.default_guess: Derive and expose every edge’s current state whenever a run is returned or inspected, without persisting it.

open_points.subject: A13 meaning of an enabled edge after its target has concluded
open_points.text: The new table calls `enabled` a “Delivery” state and defines it solely from the source and guard, but it does not say whether an enabled edge actually delivers when its target node has already concluded `upstream_failed` or `skipped_by_guard` because of another input.
open_points.question: Is `enabled` only a source-and-guard classification, or must its value still be delivered to a target that has already concluded, and if delivered where is that late input represented given the immutable NodeExecution?
options: `enabled` is only eligibility; concluded targets receive nothing
The value is delivered to concluded targets but does not alter their immutable records or conclusions
A target may not conclude until every incoming edge has ceased being `undecided`
open_points.default_guess: Treat `enabled` as eligibility and do not deliver to a target that has already concluded.
